style: point the listener to one word to listen for

candidates.angle: Asakta: unattached, the word that shows Krishna stands apart from creation
Udasinavat: like one indifferent, the word that explains how he watches creation
The verb nibadhnanti: do not bind, the word that tells us creation does not hold him

angle_en: Asakta: the word that shows Krishna stands apart
angle_hi: असक्त: शब्द जो बताता है कि कृष्ण इनसे अलग हैं

en.intro: Krishna has just described how he creates the world again and again. Now he tells Arjuna that these actions do not bind him. Listen for the word that shows how he stands apart.
en.notice: Listen for the word asakta, unattached. Krishna says he remains asakta, unattached, in those actions, which means he does not cling to the creation he himself releases into the world.
en.next: He follows this by saying he sits as a spectator, udasinavat, like one who is indifferent to what unfolds before him.
en.meaning: Those actions of creation do not bind me, Dhananjaya, because I remain detached and indifferent to them.

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने अभी-अभी बताया है कि वे बार-बार इस संसार को कैसे रचते हैं। अब वे अर्जुन से कहते हैं कि ये कर्म उन्हें बाँधते नहीं हैं। सुनिए, वह शब्द जो बताता है कि वे इनसे कैसे अलग हैं।
hi.meaning: हे धनञ्जय, वे कर्माणि मुझे बाँधते नहीं हैं, क्योंकि मैं उनमें उदासीनवत् आसीन और असक्त रहता हूँ।
hi.notice: असक्त शब्द सुनिए, जिसका अर्थ है अनासक्त। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि मैं उन कर्मों में असक्त रहता हूँ, जिसका अर्थ है कि वे स्वयं इस सृष्टि को तो रचते हैं, फिर भी उससे कोई आसक्ति नहीं रखते।
hi.next: वे आगे कहते हैं कि वे एक उदासीन दर्शक की तरह, जो कुछ हो रहा है उससे अलग, बैठे रहते हैं।

issues: meaning_changed: "हे धनञ्जय, वे सृष्टिरचना आदि कर्म मुझे बाँधते नहीं हैं, क्योंकि मैं उनमें उदासीन की तरह आसीन और असक्त रहता हूँ।" (The Hindi meaning changes the Sanskrit 'उदासीनवत्' (like one indifferent) to 'उदासीन की तरह आसीन' (sitting like an indifferent one), which shifts the meaning from 'as if indifferent' to 'sitting like an indifferent person'. More importantly, the word order 'उदासीन की तरह आसीन और असक्त' incorrectly places 'उदासीन' as a noun (the indifferent one) rather than an adjective describing Krishna's state of being, contradicting the Sanskrit 'उदासीनवत्' (like one indifferent) and 'आसीनम्' (remaining).)

unsupported: "हे धनञ्जय, वे सृष्टिरचना आदि कर्म मुझे बाँधते नहीं हैं, क्योंकि मैं उनमें उदासीन की तरह आसीन और असक्त रहता हूँ।" (The Hindi translation adds 'सृष्टिरचना आदि' (creation etc.) to 'कर्माणि', which is not in the Sanskrit source (which simply says 'those actions').)
